To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the t-PINE representation learning algorithm is able to: 1) learn explicit node representations, which are more predictable and interpretable than baseline methods; 2) learn implicit node representations, which provide a better understanding of the data; 3) learn more accurate representations for node classification tasks, compared to baseline methods, by up to 159% with respect to the Micro-F1 metric.

t-PINE is a novel approach that learns explicit and implicit node embeddings from a multi-view information network; the learned node embeddings are highly predictable, and interpretable, which allows us to exclude unrelated node embeddings.

1) the multi-view approach is more useful than the single-view approach, in terms of prediction and interpretability; 2) the implicit and explicit mapping is a good way to learn interpretable node representations; 3) the explicit representation is the most important for prediction, but the implicit representation is the most useful for visualization and interpretability.
